searchText: Goerli does anyone know a nice tool that i can run and get reports of how my internet looks over a period of time? i have a suspicion my network is being throttled / going down over night A while back I setup a tiny little server hardwired to my modem that just had Grafana, InfluxDB, and a tiny little tool that just pinged a bunch of well known endpoints (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, google.com, local ISP IP, etc.) every second and reporting the timing to Influx. Then I could just look at a chart on Grafana and outages showed up plain as day. I see It was *kinda* custom, but I didn't have to write any software IIRC. It was just a docker compose file with everything I think. If this interests you I can try to dig up the docker-compose file. I still have the machine somewhere, but I don't actually know if it is still running or not. If not, I won't bother finding it. nah it's all good, i can also wire something up if it comes to that Anyone have references on what failure modes can happen with PoS consensus protocols that have a bias towards the stake weight of older validators, making newer ones weaker for the same amount of stake? Ping with one-minute interval is probably the simplest and nicest tool you can use 😄 Just leave it running overnight, and you have the results
